title: Unramifiedness at a rational point is surjectivity on cotangent spaces
statement: Let f:X\to Y be a morphism locally of finite type between schemes over a field k [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let x\in X and y=f(x) be closed points with residue fields equal to k. Then f is unramified at x [def-weil-unramified-morphism] if and only if the induced k-linear map on cotangent spaces [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space] \mathfrak m_y/\mathfrak m_y^2\to\mathfrak m_x/\mathfrak m_x^2 is surjective.

source.place: Varieties, lemma-injective-tangent-spaces-unramified, together with the local characterization of unramified morphisms by vanishing relative differentials

proof.text: Put A = O_{Y,f(x)} and C = O_{X,x}, with the local homomorphism phi = f.stalkMap x. LocallyOfFiniteType.stalkMap gives that phi is essentially of finite type. The equality f ≫ pY = pX and surjectivity of the residue-field map of pX imply that kappa(f(x)) → kappa(x) is surjective, by Scheme.residueFieldMap_comp. Composing with the quotient A → kappa(f(x)) proves that A → kappa(x) is surjective.

source.place: lemma-injective-tangent-spaces-unramified; local differential criterion, with Mathlib Unramified/LocalRing and Stacks Tag 02GF

proof.text: Prove the local-ring criterion. In the formally unramified direction Mathlib Algebra.FormallyUnramified.map_maximalIdeal gives m_A C = m_C. Induct on membership in the ideal generated by phi(m_A). Classes of generators lift directly. For a scalar b in C, choose a in A with the same residue as b using the preceding surjectivity; (phi(a)-b)c lies in m_C squared for c in m_C. Thus every class in m_C/m_C squared lifts along the cotangent map.

source.place: lemma-injective-tangent-spaces-unramified; local differential criterion, with Mathlib Unramified/LocalRing and Stacks Tag 02GF

proof.text: Conversely, suppose the cotangent map is surjective. Since A → kappa(C) is surjective, its module of differentials is zero. The Jacobi–Zariski exact sequence therefore makes delta: m_C/m_C squared → kappa(C) tensor_C Omega_{C/A} surjective. On a class coming from m_A, delta is 1 tensor d(phi(a)) = 0. Surjectivity of the cotangent map implies delta is zero, so its target is zero. Omega_{C/A} is finite because C/A is essentially of finite type; Mathlib IsLocalRing.subsingleton_tensorProduct, the finite-module Nakayama lemma, now gives Omega_{C/A} = 0, or formal unramifiedness.

source.place: lemma-injective-tangent-spaces-unramified; local differential criterion, with Mathlib Unramified/LocalRing and Stacks Tag 02GF

proof.text: An open neighbourhood on which the diagonal is an open immersion is formally unramified, and hence its stalk map is formally unramified by Mathlib FormallyUnramified.stalkMap. Cancel the stalk isomorphism of the open immersion to get formal unramifiedness of f.stalkMap x. Conversely apply lem-sbc-formally-unramified-stalk-neighbourhood; restriction preserves locally finite type, and Mathlib FormallyUnramified.isOpenImmersion_diagonal supplies the required diagonal. Combining with the local-ring equivalence proves the unchanged theorem.

lean.statement: theorem rational_unramified_iff_cotangent_surjective (k : Type u) [Field k] (X Y : Scheme.{u}) (pX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (pY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (f : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (hf : f ≫ pY = pX) (x : X) (hx : IsClosed ({x} : Set X)) (hy : IsClosed ({f x} : Set Y)) (hκx : Function.Bijective (pX.residueFieldMap x).hom) (hκy : Function.Bijective (pY.residueFieldMap (f x)).hom) : (∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType (U.ι ≫ f) ∧ IsOpenImmersion (pullback.diagonal (U.ι ≫ f))) ↔ Function.Surjective (Ideal.mapCotangent (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Y.presheaf.stalk (f x))) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (f.stalkMap x).hom.toIntAlgHom (Ideal.map_le_iff_le_comap.mp (IsLocalRing.map_maximalIdeal_le (f.stalkMap x).hom)) : IsLocalRing.CotangentSpace (Y.presheaf.stalk (f x)) →ₗ[ℤ] IsLocalRing.CotangentSpace (X.presheaf.stalk x))
